title: RECEIPT
description: Work reported done. One file per completed dispatch in workflow/receipts/, named <date>-<short-slug>.md. Human form: workflow/templates/RECEIPT.md. Machine form: the FIELD: value lines of that file, parsed as scripts/onboard_check.py parses them. 'Done' without evidence is not a state (Law 5).

filled.description: A required field must be present, non-empty, and not still hold a <template placeholder>.

STATE.description: DONE | PARTIAL | BLOCKED | KILLED | INVALIDATED. Compared case-insensitively (the checker uppercases before matching).

EXACT_REF.description: Commit/artifact hash the evidence was produced against. If it is a 7-40 hex string and the tree is a git clone, the checker requires that commit to exist.

EVIDENCE.description: Command output, file path, hash, or measurement that proves the state -- something a verifier can re-run or re-read.

PROGRESS.description: DECISION | MEASUREMENT | INFRASTRUCTURE. Compared case-insensitively. A DONE or KILLED receipt claiming DECISION or MEASUREMENT progress may not have an EFFECT beginning with 'none'.

EFFECT.description: The decision changed or measured outcome; use 'none -- infrastructure' honestly.

BLOCKED_ON.description: Only if BLOCKED: the precise missing thing and who owns it. The template lists it; the checker requires it only when STATE is BLOCKED.

SESSION_ID.description: The session/transcript identifier that produced this work -- required for receipts dated 2026-08-09 or later; makes every verdict pairable to its trajectory. The date lives in the filename, so the checker (not this schema) enforces the cutoff.

ACTUAL.description: Optional but expected when the dispatch carried a FORECAST: actual duration / tokens / attempts -- the flywheel grades forecast vs actual.

NEXT_OWNER.description: Who/what consumes this: a seat, the lead, a gate, 'none -- terminal'.
